title: Nap-Transition Readiness by Wake Window
dataSources: Baby feedings (`baby:feed`), baby sleep (`baby:sleep`), diaper changes (`diaper:change`), school departures (`school:departure`), stroller activity (`stroller:walk`), household chores (`chore:event`), and family geofence events (`family:location`).
app: Family and baby telemetry from baby-tracking apps, school and geofence automations, stroller logs, chore trackers, and shared-home events streamed to Splunk HEC via APIs and Home Assistant.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=baby:sleep event="nap_start"
| stats avg(wake_window_min) as avg_wake_window_min avg(sleep_minutes) as avg_nap_minutes by child nap_number
| sort child nap_number
description: Compares wake-window length with the quality of the following nap to show when the nap schedule is ready to shift.
value: Nap transitions are easier when you can see the wake windows that still produce good sleep instead of relying on vague intuition.
implementation: Capture nap starts with the preceding wake-window duration from your baby-tracking app.
visualization: Line chart of average wake window and nap duration by nap number.
grandmaExplanation: It spots how long your child stays awake before a nap and whether that timing still seems to work well.
